title: Low-level design
description: Turn requirements into clear responsibilities, interfaces, and collaborating objects.

modules.title: Responsibilities & object models
modules.description: Turn requirements into clear responsibilities, interfaces, and collaborating objects.

lessons.title: Start with responsibilities
lessons.body:
### Model behavior before inheritance
List the operations the system must support. Assign each operation to a component that owns the information and rules it needs.

For a parking lot, allocating a compatible spot is different from calculating a fee. Keeping these responsibilities separate makes each policy easier to change.

### State invariants
A spot cannot hold two active vehicles. A closed ticket cannot be closed again. Make these rules explicit before choosing class names.

lessons.title: Interfaces & composition
lessons.body:
### Introduce a boundary for real variation
A fee policy can vary independently of ticket storage. An interface can let a parking service ask a fee policy for a price without knowing its implementation.

### Prefer small collaborators
Compose a service from a spot allocator, a ticket store, and a fee policy. Avoid a single class that owns persistence, allocation, pricing, and user interaction.

An interface has a cost. Introduce one where it expresses a useful contract or isolates an expected change.

exercises.title: Build a parking lot service
exercises.prompt: Complete allocation, ticket creation, and exit handling. There is one car spot and one motorcycle spot; only matching vehicles may park. Return -1 when full, for unknown or closed tickets, or when exit precedes entry. Use monotonically increasing ticket IDs. The hourly fee is 10 units per whole hour; the flat fee is 15. Run the supplied scenario and compare stdout with the expected output. Explain how pricing can change independently of allocation.
hints: Allocate only a free spot of the requested type.
Validate the ticket and exit time before changing state.
A successful exit closes the ticket and releases its spot; the injected policy calculates the fee.
exercises.expected:
Car ticket: 1
Second car: -1
Motorcycle ticket: 2
Early exit: -1
Car fee: 30
Repeated exit: -1
New car ticket: 3
Flat fee: 15
